children.objective: Prioritize a single-thread, output-stationary blocked GEMM as a kernel experiment: retain small C tiles in registers, vectorize across contiguous output columns, and tune register/cache blocking and unrolling without first adding parallel complexity. Keep dynamic n handling, including fringes. Measure this kernel at both thread budgets (it may use one worker at either) so its benefit can be distinguished from threading and considered for later combination. Use explicit intrinsics only when supported by the actual build, or retain a safe general path. Validate correctness and wall-clock time across the timed cases and preserve correctness for every valid size; other correctness-preserving experiments remain possible.
children.subject: Direct output-stationary SIMD kernel, isolated from thread scaling

children.objective: Explore the alternative of transposing or packing B into per-call scratch so each output dot product can use contiguous k-wise loads and SIMD reductions. Measure whether the transform cost pays off at the tested sizes and thread budgets; parallelize independent output rows or row groups within the threads limit. Do not reuse cached data or specialize to n=384/768. Check signed-input correctness against the FP64 tolerance, including the changed reduction order, and preserve a correct general-n path.
children.subject: Per-call B transpose/packing with k-wise SIMD reductions

children.objective: Prioritize OpenMP decomposition and thread scaling around a cache-aware, compiler-vectorizable i-k-j row-major loop: initialize C, then update contiguous C row segments from contiguous B rows, assigning independent row slabs or 2D output tiles to workers. Compare these decompositions, static scheduling, and parallel-region overhead, with a serial path when the budget is one. This contrasts with T1's output-stationary kernel and T2's transformed-B reduction approach. Respect the thread budget, keep n dynamic, measure all timed cases, and validate the full-output overwrite and numerical tolerance. Treat the loop form as the main hypothesis, not a restriction on correctness-preserving experiments.
children.subject: Row-owned i-k-j loop and OpenMP decomposition

created_trees.objective: À partir du candidat SIMD T2 mesuré, explorer le parallélisme OpenMP sur les sorties (lignes ou tuiles), sans réduction sur K, pour exploiter le budget de quatre threads tout en conservant une voie à un thread. Mesurer n=384 et 768 avec les budgets 1 et 4; inclure les coûts de lancement, traiter les bords et toutes les tailles valides, respecter la tolérance et réécrire toute la sortie. N’utiliser que l’ISA activée par la compilation et éviter les seuils particuliers aux tailles de test.

children.objective: Explore a single-thread, cache-friendly row-major GEMM using loop interchange and cache blocking, with tile sizes that work across arbitrary n and correct handling of edge tiles. Keep this branch free of explicit SIMD intrinsics, panel packing, and OpenMP so it isolates locality and compiler auto-vectorization. Ensure every output element is assigned on every call, validate against the FP64 oracle for all supported sizes, and compare official timings at both timed sizes with one thread.
children.subject: Single-thread cache locality and loop blocking

children.objective: Explore an explicit register-tiled FP32 SIMD microkernel, using the ISA enabled for the supplied target; assess whether packing panels is worthwhile with its allocation and copy costs included. Keep this branch single-threaded to isolate kernel throughput. Handle arbitrary dimensions and edge tiles, overwrite all output elements, preserve the required FP32 tolerance for signed inputs, and measure both timed sizes with one thread.
children.subject: Explicit SIMD microkernel and panel packing

children.objective: Focus on OpenMP scaling and output ownership. With one fixed correct compute kernel per comparison, compare static row-stripe partitioning with static 2D output-tile ownership; avoid K-splitting reductions and global OpenMP state changes, and never exceed the caller's thread budget. Measure one and four threads at both timed sizes, including overhead. Keep kernel design fixed while comparing partition policies so this does not become a second broad single-thread kernel-tuning effort. Validate all supported sizes, preserve the FP32 tolerance, and overwrite the full output on every call.
children.subject: OpenMP scaling and output ownership
